title: Consistency Models
summary: Consistency models specify what observations clients may make. From linearizability to eventual consistency, each model enables and forbids certain anomalies — learn them to pick storage and API guarantees.

sections.title: Linearizability and sequential consistency
paragraphs: Linearizability: operations appear instantaneously at a single point between invocation and response, globally. Sequential consistency allows reordering across clients but preserves each client's order.

sections.title: Causal and session models
paragraphs: Causal consistency preserves cause-before-effect. Session guarantees (read-your-writes, monotonic reads) are often what users actually need for a single device/login.

sections.title: Eventual consistency
paragraphs: If updates stop, replicas converge. During churn, stale reads and conflicts happen. Pair with conflict resolution (LWW, CRDT, app merge).

sections.title: Choosing per API
paragraphs: Payments capture may need strong guarantees; feed ranking may tolerate staleness. Document guarantees in API specs so clients do not invent them.

deepDive.title: Consistency Models — Operations
paragraphs: Operating Consistency Models in production means defining SLIs before tuning knobs, knowing amplification costs, and rehearsing failure modes.
Prefer reversible changes, feature flags, and canaries. Measure p50/p99 and error rate under load that matches production skew.
bullets: Define capacity from the scarcest resource
Keep rollback cheaper than forward repair when possible

deepDive.title: Consistency Models — Failure modes
paragraphs: Common failures around Consistency Models include overload, partial dependency outages, and silent correctness bugs that pass happy-path tests.
Inject faults in staging: latency, loss, clock skew, and disk full. Verify alerts fire and degradation is intentional.

expert.title: Consistency Models — Expert notes
paragraphs: At the expert level, Consistency Models intersects multi-region consistency, cost envelopes, and organizational constraints (team ownership, on-call load).
Write down the non-goals. Many outages come from optimizing a metric that was never the product requirement.

pitfalls: One global model for all data
keyTakeaways: Session guarantees cover many UX needs
whyItMatters: Misstated consistency is how you get heisenbugs and angry users after failover.
reflectionQuestions: Which of your APIs accidentally promise linearizability?
numbersToKnow: Know your p99 latency budget before adding hops
Peak load ≠ average load — plan headroom (often 2–3×)
Cross-region RTT is often ~50–150ms one way
